title: RESEARCH: cbor_skip integer overflow (size_t)val*2u on 32-bit targets
description: src/wp11_keystore.c line ~392: for MAP type, the skip loop iterates (size_t)val * 2u times. val is uint64_t decoded from the CBOR header. On a 32-bit platform (size_t=32bit), if val > SIZE_MAX/2 the multiplication wraps and the loop iterates far fewer times than the actual map entry count. Since cbor_skip runs on a fully AES-GCM authenticated buffer the attacker scenario requires defeating the encryption first. The practical upper bound is WP11_KEYSTORE_MAX_CT_LEN=512KB which cannot hold 2^31 map entries so this is not exploitable, but it is technically UB. Research: confirm the maximum val that can appear in a valid keystore CBOR payload; confirm whether an overflow is reachable given WP11_KEYSTORE_MAX_CT_LEN. Fix if reachable: add overflow guard before the multiplication. Add inline comment documenting the reasoning regardless.
